claims.text: The proposed approach integrates ab initio-based techniques into a Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflow.
The workflow will improve the accuracy of thermal-conductivity predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The workflow will improve the accuracy of electrical-conductivity predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The accuracy improvement will apply in the 0–200 K regime.
The accuracy improvement will apply in the 300–1200 K regime.
Explicit consideration of defect structures and oxygen impurities will improve computational modeling of thermal and electrical conductivity.
The proposed approach applies to bulk HfNbTaTiZr both without oxygen addition and with 1 wt.% oxygen.
The approach will reduce the mean absolute error of thermal- and electrical-conductivity predictions by 15% relative to existing analytical approaches.
The claimed applicability does not extend to temperatures outside 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The claimed applicability does not extend to specimens with oxygen contents outside 0–1 wt.%.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the quality of the ab initio techniques and Bayesian optimization workflow.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the availability of experimental validation data.
Conductivity measurements on specimens with and without 1 wt.% oxygen can be used to test the predictions across the stated temperature regimes.
The hypothesis is falsified if its mean absolute error is not at least 10% lower than that of existing analytical approaches.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a 15% error reduction, whereas falsification requires failure to reach only a 10% reduction. A result between 10% and 15% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
